preamble: Wordplay in all but one of the across clues is 17

clue.text: Correctly positioned current units on manoeuvres

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Army units on exercise find themselves in the right place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in its original place, so something in situ is properly placed.

clue.text: Are six fags put out? They may be in bed

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether half a dozen cigarettes have been extinguished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a flower bed, not a place to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: These alpine plants are grown in garden flower beds, so the cryptic hint describes them by location.

clue.text: Fools Sun journalist given appraisal

parts.note: asses are fools
S is short for Sunday or sun
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A tabloid writer at the Sun is reviewed by idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: To be evaluated is to receive an appraisal, so the past participle matches the phrase.

clue.text: What programmer does is computer-generated

parts.note: C stands for computer, as in the abbreviation CG for computer-generated
G stands for generated, the second half of the abbreviation CG

explanation.surface: A remark that a programmer's work is all produced by machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble the wordplay is 'godless': the Norse chief god Odin is missing from it and must be put back inside to fill the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing program instructions is the programmer's daily task, so this gerund names exactly that activity.

clue.text: Mint drink isn't quite finished in match

parts.note: to mint is to coin money

indicators.note: not quite finished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: cider is an apple drink

explanation.surface: Someone's cocktail is nearly done during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like a flavour for the drink but is a verb meaning to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: To match is to correspond or agree, which is to coincide; both verbs.

clue.text: Fancy loading packing area on a slope

indicators.note: packing means the jumbled letters take the next piece inside
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: Elaborate cargo stowing done in a storage area on sloping ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanting line runs at an angle, so something sloped lies obliquely.

clue.text: Prince with second officers

parts.note: the Roman god of war, missing from the wordplay per the preamble and restored in the grid
Hal is Prince Hal, Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: A royal accompanied by a second-in-command among his officials.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble the wordplay is 'godless': the Roman war god is absent and goes in front. Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshals are high-ranking military or law officers, so the plural noun is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Top ten introduced by a spinning record

indicators.note: introduced by means the following pieces come before it
a spinning record turns round, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A chart hit spun on vinyl enters the top ten.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or summit, so it is a synonym of the noun top.

clue.text: Band quiet after covers of Sinatra

indicators.note: after says the next piece comes behind the first
covers are the outside, so the first and last letters

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A quiet group plays after its versions of Sinatra songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' suggests cover versions of songs but means the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn around the waist or over the shoulder.

clue.text: Intelligence one's giving Arabs

parts.note: IQ, the intelligence quotient, stands for intelligence
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone's intelligence work is handed over to Arab people.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble the wordplay is 'godless': the Egyptian sun god Ra is missing and goes back in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: People of Iraq are Arabs for the most part, so this is an example given by a broader class.

clue.text: Awful quality of discs, regularly scratched

indicators.note: every other letter of discs is scratched out, leaving the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Records with periodic scratches make for dreadful sound quality.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble the wordplay is 'godless': Irene (Eirene), Greek goddess of peace, is missing and goes back in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dire is dreadful, so the noun made from it is the quality of being awful.

clue.text: Dancers rolling cigs around both hands

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters go round the next piece
rolling cigs by hand suggests reshaping these letters into a new order

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, the two hands

explanation.surface: Dancers backstage rolling their own cigarettes with both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble the wordplay is 'godless': the falcon-headed Egyptian god Horus is missing and goes back in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a stage chorus line are dancers, so the phrase is a specific example of the plural noun.

clue.text: Idea that is sweeping angry elite away

indicators.note: away suggests the letters are swept off and rearranged

explanation.surface: A notion that sweeps the furious upper class aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angry' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'away' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: A generality is a broad statement or notion, an idea that is all-encompassing.

clue.text: On average, driving aid making a good comeback?

parts.note: re means on or concerning
par is an average or standard
a tee is used to drive a golf ball

explanation.surface: An average golfing tee that makes a good recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: A witty retort is a quick reply, so the question mark flags a pun on comeback.

clue.text: Old German bread Frank's putting away quietly

indicators.note: putting away means the next letter is removed

parts.note: franks are postal stamps, so the plural of postmark
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A German loaf that Frank tucks away silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, and Frank is no person here.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the currency of East Germany, and money is slang-called bread.

clue.text: Old man welcomes card player with poker face

indicators.note: welcomes means the first word takes another inside it

parts.note: old man is slang for father, so dad
in bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so E is a card player
the Greek god of the wild, left out of the wordplay and restored in the grid

explanation.surface: A father greets a card player who keeps an expressionless face.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble the wordplay is 'godless': Pan, Greek god of the wild, is missing from it. In bridge, East is one of the four players.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan delivery shows no emotion, just like a poker player's unreadable face, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Set out to break part of bike stand

indicators.note: to break means the next piece splits the first apart

parts.note: a pedal is part of a bike

indicators.note: out signals the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to break a bicycle stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'out' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is a base or plinth on which something stands, so it is a stand.

clue.text: Lacking faith in vessel, do glide westwards

indicators.note: westwards says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An unbeliever aboard a ship, gliding off towards the west.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the one across clue whose wordplay keeps everything; 'in' marks the hidden letters, and 'westwards' turns them right to left in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without belief in a deity has no religious faith, so the adjective matches.

clue.text: Crazy investing sadly returning capital once

indicators.note: returning says the combined letters are read backwards
investing means wrapping round, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: mad means crazy
alas is an exclamation said sadly

explanation.surface: A wild and unhappy investment returning money from an old capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the whole of MAAL ASD round. Per the preamble the wordplay is 'godless': Ares, Greek god of war, goes back in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This Tanzanian city was the country's capital until Dodoma replaced it, hence a former capital.

clue.text: Dave stripped, given a rating for divine figure

indicators.note: stripped means the outer letters are removed

parts.note: a rating is a naval sailor, also called a tar

explanation.surface: Dave undressed and received a rating on a god-like figure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism an avatar is the incarnation of a deity on earth, so a divine figure.

clue.text: You'll be sent on a trip by this leader of air force

definitions.text: You'll be sent on a trip by this

indicators.note: leader of means take the first letter

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, a police force

explanation.surface: An air force commander sends you on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' is a hallucinatory experience, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: LSD, the hallucinogen, is called acid, and taking it gives a trip.

clue.text: Adult writing about love in book

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: MS is manuscript, writing
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: An adult writing about love in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a prophetic book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Turned up clutching one lady's undergarment

indicators.note: clutching means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: turned up means arrived, came
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone arrived holding a woman's slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like a reversal sign but simply means arrived. Per the preamble the wordplay is 'godless': Sol, the Roman sun god, goes back in.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a sleeveless women's top worn beneath clothing, so it is an example of lingerie.

clue.text: Person sacrificed sheep the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
the Norse god of war, missing from the wordplay and restored in the grid

explanation.surface: A victim offered up after a sheep went astray.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble the wordplay is 'godless': Tyr, the Norse god of war, is absent from it and completes the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is put to death for their beliefs, someone sacrificed for a cause.

clue.text: Feeling of aversion in country, moving south-east

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, left out of the wordplay and restored in the grid

indicators.note: moving means a letter is shifted to a new place in the word
east says the letter travels rightwards, towards the end

parts.note: a state is a country
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Disgust felt in a nation going through a south-eastward migration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south-east' reads as a compass point but splits: south 'moving' 'east' within the country word. Dis, Roman god of the underworld, is missing per the preamble and goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is dislike or repugnance, a mild feeling of aversion, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Computer's flipping small parts on screen

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over, reading it backwards

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer; the 's is just the link 'is'
Eos is the Greek goddess of dawn, left out of the wordplay and restored in the grid

explanation.surface: A computer is flipping through tiny clips on a monitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble the wordplay is 'godless': Eos, the Greek goddess of dawn, is missing and follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameos are brief appearances by well-known actors in film, small roles on screen.
